record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: Let f be a superattracting germ in End(C^n, O) with first nonzero homogeneous term H, and suppose the postcritical set of f is a topological cone near the origin. Under what additional conditions is f topologically locally conjugate to H? In particular, is the answer always yes when H is non-degenerate?

evidence.quote: (OP8) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be a superattracting germ ... Assume that the postcritical set of f is a topological cone nearby the origin. Under which conditions is then f topologically locally conjugated to H? In particular, is this true when H is non-degenerate?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, written as $f = H + (\text{higher order terms})$, where $H$ is the first nonzero homogeneous term of $f$ at $O$ and $\deg H \geq 2$ (so that $O$ is a superattracting fixed point of $f$). Recall that $H$ is called non-degenerate if $H^{-1}(O) = \{O\}$. Let $\mathrm{Crit}(f)$ denote the critical set of $f$ (the zero locus of $\det df$), and define the postcritical set as $\mathrm{PC}(f) = \bigcup_{k\geq 1} f^k(\mathrm{Crit}(f))$. A subset $S \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is a topological cone near $O$ if there is a neighborhood $U$ of $O$ and a homeomorphism $\Phi$ of $U$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb{C}^n$ sending $S \cap U$ to a union of straight rays emanating from $O$.

Assume that $\mathrm{PC}(f)$ is a topological cone near $O$. Determine additional conditions on $f$ (or on $H$) under which $f$ is topologically locally conjugate to $H$ at $O$, i.e., there exists a germ of homeomorphism $\varphi : (\mathbb{C}^n, O) \to (\mathbb{C}^n, O)$ with $\varphi \circ f = H \circ \varphi$ near $O$. In particular, decide whether such a topological local conjugacy always exists when $H$ is non-degenerate.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question on local discrete holomorphic dynamics in several complex variables. Standard references on Böttcher-type coordinates at superattracting fixed points (Buff–Epstein–Koch and others) treat the non-degenerate homogeneous case under additional hypotheses but do not establish a general topological local conjugacy of $f$ to its leading homogeneous part $H$ from the topological cone condition on the postcritical set alone. No published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Böttcher coordinates (Buff, Epstein, Koch)
status_evidence.snippet: Germs of analytic maps with an adapted superattracting fixed point at the origin... critical and postcritical loci are cones over critical sets in the homogeneous nondegenerate case.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related work treats Böttcher-type linearization/conjugacy of superattracting germs to homogeneous models under additional structural conditions, but does not settle the cone-criterion question in general.

status_evidence.title: Böttcher coordinates at superattracting fixed points (AMS ECGD)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs Böttcher coordinates conjugating skew product superattracting germs to monomial maps under suitable weight conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Available results give topological/holomorphic conjugacy to the homogeneous part only under specific hypotheses, leaving the general topological cone criterion unresolved.
